suggestions.plain: This word is not in the dictionary, so it may be a typo. Scientific terms, names and abbreviations are usually recognised. If it is a real word you use, add it to your dictionary from this card and it will not be flagged again.
suggestions.why: Spelling against a frequency dictionary plus a scientific lexicon (seroprevalence, covariates, nowcasting are not errors here). Proper nouns, acronyms and UK/US variants are skipped. A word used three or more times is flagged at every use only when it is a known kind of slip next to a common word (a learned error model of real misspellings); any other repeated word is asked about once instead. A false alarm on your own terminology: 'Add to dictionary' on the card teaches it the word.
suggestions.source: SymSpell spelling engine with Researchly's scientific lexicon

suggestions.plain: This phrase can be shorter: 'because' instead of 'due to the fact that'. Shorter is easier to read, and the meaning stays the same.
suggestions.why: Cut ruthlessly, but second: on a revision pass, try to remove ten per cent of the words without losing meaning. You almost always can, and the prose tightens every time.
suggestions.source: The Craft of Scientific Writing (Researchly's founding guide): Language and tone

suggestions.plain: A word is repeated by accident, like 'the the'. Delete one.
suggestions.why: A mechanical slip the eye forgives and the reader stumbles on; the read-aloud test catches these.
suggestions.source: The Craft of Scientific Writing (Researchly's founding guide): A practical workflow to beat the blank page
